description: Is ingestion keeping up, and is it correct? RED for the five consumers, then throughput, latency, correctness and runtime.

panels.title: Messages consumed/s
panels.description: Rate. Messages the Kafka client handed to the consumers, per second, over the last minute.

panels.title: Rows inserted in range
panels.description: Rows the inserts committed over the selected time range. Below the messages consumed means duplicates or poison messages.

targets.expr: sum((sum by (job) (rows_inserted_total{job=~"$job"}) - sum by (job) (rows_inserted_total{job=~"$job"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (rows_inserted_total{job=~"$job"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: DLQ messages in range (S4)
panels.description: Errors. Messages sent to the dead-letter topic over the selected range. S4: zero. Any value means a poison message: see DLQ by reason below.

targets.expr: sum((sum by (job) (dlq_messages_total{job=~"$job"}) - sum by (job) (dlq_messages_total{job=~"$job"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (dlq_messages_total{job=~"$job"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Fallback verdicts in range
panels.description: Errors. Committed rows no rule matched, over the selected range. Any value is a ruleset authoring bug: a source with no source_default rule.

targets.expr: sum((sum by (job) (categorization_verdicts_total{job=~"$job", matcher_type="fallback"}) - sum by (job) (categorization_verdicts_total{job=~"$job", matcher_type="fallback"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (categorization_verdicts_total{job=~"$job", matcher_type="fallback"})) or vector(0)

panels.title: Ingest lag p95 in range (S2)
panels.description: Duration. 95th percentile of insert time minus the Kafka record timestamp, over the selected range. S2: under 5 s.

panels.title: Consumers down
panels.description: Consumers Prometheus could not scrape on its last attempt. A down consumer raises no errors: its source just goes quiet.

panels.title: Rate: messages consumed/s
panels.description: Messages the Kafka client handed to each consumer, per second.

panels.title: Errors: DLQ messages/s
panels.description: Messages each consumer sent to the dead-letter topic, per second. A flat zero is healthy; the breakdown by reason is under Correctness.

panels.title: Duration: ingest lag p95 (S2)
panels.description: Insert time minus the Kafka record timestamp, 95th percentile per consumer. S2: under 5 s (red line). Gaps mean no traffic.

panels.title: Messages consumed per window
panels.description: Messages each consumer took from Kafka in each window, exact. A bar labelled 09:00 counts 08:50 to 09:00; the window in progress appears once it closes. The Bucket picker sets the window; a long time range widens it to keep the bars readable.

targets.expr: (sum by (job) (kafka_consumed_messages{job=~"$job"}) - sum by (job) (kafka_consumed_messages{job=~"$job"} offset $__interval)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (kafka_consumed_messages{job=~"$job"})

panels.title: Rows inserted per window
panels.description: Rows each consumer committed in each window, exact. Lower than consumed means duplicates, poison messages or tombstones. A bar labelled 09:00 counts 08:50 to 09:00.

targets.expr: (sum by (job) (rows_inserted_total{job=~"$job"}) - sum by (job) (rows_inserted_total{job=~"$job"} offset $__interval)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (rows_inserted_total{job=~"$job"})

panels.title: Totals in range by consumer
panels.description: Exact counts over the selected time range. Consumed should equal inserted + duplicates + DLQ + tombstones, give or take a batch still in flight. A consumer that restarted inside the range counts from its restart.

targets.expr: (sum by (job) (kafka_consumed_messages{job=~"$job"}) - sum by (job) (kafka_consumed_messages{job=~"$job"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (kafka_consumed_messages{job=~"$job"}) or sum by (job) (up{job=~"$job"} * 0)

(sum by (job) (rows_inserted_total{job=~"$job"}) - sum by (job) (rows_inserted_total{job=~"$job"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (rows_inserted_total{job=~"$job"}) or sum by (job) (up{job=~"$job"} * 0)

(sum by (job) (duplicates_skipped_total{job=~"$job"}) - sum by (job) (duplicates_skipped_total{job=~"$job"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (duplicates_skipped_total{job=~"$job"}) or sum by (job) (up{job=~"$job"} * 0)

(sum by (job) (dlq_messages_total{job=~"$job"}) - sum by (job) (dlq_messages_total{job=~"$job"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (dlq_messages_total{job=~"$job"}) or sum by (job) (up{job=~"$job"} * 0)

(sum by (job) (tombstones_skipped_total{job=~"$job"}) - sum by (job) (tombstones_skipped_total{job=~"$job"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or sum by (job) (tombstones_skipped_total{job=~"$job"}) or sum by (job) (up{job=~"$job"} * 0)

panels.title: Rows inserted/s
panels.description: Rows committed per second. Below messages consumed/s means duplicates or poison messages.

panels.title: Flushes by trigger
panels.description: Why each batch was flushed. Mostly linger: batches don't fill (low load). Mostly size: saturated. Pick one consumer in the job picker to see its own mix.

panels.title: Batch size p50 / p95
panels.description: Messages per flush. Solid line p95, dashed line p50.

panels.title: Flush duration p95
panels.description: A whole flush: handling the batch, then committing its offsets. Rising while insert duration stays flat means the time goes outside the database.

panels.title: Insert duration p95
panels.description: The batch insert's database transaction only.

panels.title: Kafka lag: messages behind per partition
panels.description: Mean of the client's per-partition lag samples (latest offset minus committed), taken every lag-monitoring interval. Rising means the consumer is falling behind. A mean, not a percentile: the client's histogram uses default buckets that stop at 10, so a quantile would never read above 10 messages.

panels.title: Duplicates skipped/s
panels.description: Rows skipped by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Non-zero under CHAOS_DUPLICATE_PCT, or on a re-send of the same records, is correct behaviour (S3).

panels.title: DLQ by reason
panels.description: Dead-letter messages per second by consumer and reason. Shows No data until the first poison message.

panels.title: Verdicts by matcher tier
panels.description: Which matcher tier decided each committed row. A growing source_default share means a rule-coverage gap; any fallback is a ruleset bug.

panels.title: Tombstones skipped/s
panels.description: Null-value records skipped by design.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Process CPU time per second. 100% is one full core.

panels.title: Resident memory
panels.description: Process resident set size. Climbing without levelling off under steady load points to a leak.

panels.title: Event loop lag p99
panels.description: How late the event loop runs scheduled work. High lag with high CPU means the consumer is CPU-bound.

panels.title: Slow batches
panels.description: consume.batch traces over 1 s. Click a trace id to open its timeline. Empty is healthy. Needs OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=false (make up-all).
